A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModeSeq work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references and two-page supplementary material are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WOMD and Argoverse 2 experiments, decoder and training ablations, mode-extrapolation results, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds single-model WOMD test results and experiments using alternative scene encoders.

M1.justification: Sequential decoding, Memory and Context Transformers, mode rearrangement, EMTA training and Weighted Trajectory Fusion remain unchanged. Alternative-encoder experiments instantiate the existing framework; no new decoding component or training rule is specified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate motion forecasting on WOMD and Argoverse 2. The additional encoder comparisons and single-model results use retained datasets and tasks, without introducing new populations, domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 supplementary Table 6 adds evaluated Scene Transformer and HiVT baselines, each compared with its ModeSeq-equipped counterpart. These methods were cited but not evaluated as comparators in v1. Existing benchmark and ablation comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds alternative-encoder configurations trained on 20% of WOMD and evaluated on validation data, plus a single-model WOMD test condition. Previously stated splits, prediction horizons, metrics, training budgets and standard model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New supplementary Section 8 tests whether ModeSeq's benefits extend beyond the QCNet encoder, using Scene Transformer and HiVT. Section 9 adds a parameter-efficiency comparison. Existing training, rearrangement, refinement and mode-extrapolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The same latency values and their ± quantities move from v1 supplementary Table 6 into v2 Table 5. Neither version supplies additional seed counts, repeated-run information or statistical tests for prediction performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds single-model WOMD test scores, including Soft mAP6 0.4487, mAP6 0.4450 and MR6 0.1244. New Table 6 reports alternative-encoder results, including mAP6 0.4095 for Scene Transformer + ModeSeq and 0.4086 for HiVT + ModeSeq. Existing scores and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(12) retain the same substantive definitions and operations, including EMTA assignment and matching thresholds. Changing the decoding index from t to k and rewriting the factorization notation are equivalent restatements. No theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The central claims about sequential mode modeling, EMTA, balanced prediction and mode extrapolation remain. Section 4.2 nevertheless recasts the first-place claim from the submission-time WOMD leaderboard to the 2024 Waymo challenge, a limited change in the stated scope of competitive performance.

C2.justification: v2 expands explanations of confidence scoring and mAP behavior, quantifies the existing EMTA accuracy tradeoff, and explicitly limits EMTA to ordered mode embeddings. It removes v1's qualification that joint multi-agent prediction remains unvalidated, while retaining the latency limitation in the main experiments.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes map contours and semantic tags, trajectory bounding-box inputs, and confidence scores that need not sum to one. Supplementary Section 9 discloses 7.5M decoder parameters and 10.9M total parameters with QCNet. These are additional disclosures, without an established change to the original implementation.

R1.justification: Removing the set-prediction motivation also removes citations to DAB-DETR, Conditional DETR, Deformable DETR and Order Matters: Sequence to Sequence for Sets. Most motion-prediction positioning remains intact; v2 additionally positions ModeSeq as parameter-efficient relative to MTR and MTR++.

P1.justification: Section 3 removes the standalone Motivation discussion and places Scene Encoding before Sequential Mode Decoding. Local explanations and terminology are revised, latency discussion moves into Section 4.3, and supplementary sections are reorganized. The overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 rebuilds Table 5 to combine prediction quality with the relocated latency measurements, introduces the encoder-comparison Table 6, and expands Table 1. Table captions, widths and row groupings are revised. All six figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: Supplementary Table 6 substantiates the previously asserted encoder flexibility, while Table 1 adds useful single-model test evidence. Combining latency with prediction quality and disclosing parameter counts improves assessment of practical costs. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the explicit joint-prediction limitation; the central method and established results remain unchanged.
